correct_completion: it will have to be accepted by every department.
full_sentence: Whatever the committee ultimately decides, it will have to be accepted by every department.
acceptable_variants: it must be respected by all departments.
every department will need to follow it.

options.text: so the department has already rejected it.
options.why_wrong: This gives a past-tense result, which does not match the future-oriented meaning of the free relative clause 'whatever... decides'.

options.text: it will have to be accepted by every department.
the committee has been meeting since May.
options.why_wrong: This adds background information but does not complete the main clause that the 'whatever' clause requires.

options.text: all departments were consulted last year.
options.why_wrong: The past tense describes an earlier event, while the stem points to a future consequence of the decision.

grammar_focus: Free relative clauses with 'whatever' as the subject of a sentence
explanation: A clause introduced by 'whatever' functions as a nominal subject, so the main clause must give the predicate that applies to it. Speakers of Spanish often add a conditional or subjunctive marker here, but English requires a plain modal construction after the free relative clause.
translation: Lo que sea que decida finalmente el comité tendrá que ser aceptado por todos los departamentos.
